claim: Central Europe is experiencing more frequent and prolonged periods of drought in the course of global climate change.
source: In the course of global climate change, Central Europe is experiencing more frequent and prolonged periods of drought.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Christensen et al., 2007).

claim: The drought years 2018 and 2019 affected European beeches (Fagus sylvatica L.) differently, with drought-damaged trees neighbouring healthy trees even in the same stand.
source: The drought years 2018 and 2019 affected European beeches (Fagus sylvatica L.) differently: even in the same stand, drought-damaged trees neighboured healthy trees
evidence: This observation is described in the abstract and elaborated in the introduction with supporting data.

claim: The genotype rather than the environment was responsible for the conspicuous pattern of differential drought damage in beech trees.
source: even in the same stand, drought-damaged trees neighboured healthy trees, suggesting that the genotype rather than the environment was responsible for this conspicuous pattern.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the abstract and supported by the GWAS findings showing genetic associations with drought phenotypes.

claim: Pool-GWAS identified 106 significantly associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) throughout the genome.
source: Contrasting the extreme phenotypes identified 106 significantly associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) throughout the genome.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by the GWAS results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Most annotated genes with associated SNPs (>70%) were previously implicated in the drought reaction of plants.
source: Most annotated genes with associated SNPs (>70%) were previously implicated in the drought reaction of plants.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the gene function analysis in Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Non-synonymous substitutions led either to a functional amino acid exchange or premature termination.
source: Non-synonymous substitutions led either to a functional amino acid exchange or premature termination.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and detailed in Table 1 showing specific amino acid changes.

claim: A non-parametric machine learning approach on 98 validation samples yielded 20 informative loci which allowed an 88% prediction probability of the drought phenotype.
source: A non-parametric machine learning approach on 98 validation samples yielded 20 informative loci which allowed an 88% prediction probability of the drought phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and detailed in the genomic prediction results section.

claim: Drought resistance in European beech is a moderately polygenic trait that should respond well to natural selection, selective management, and breeding.
source: Drought resistance in European beech is a moderately polygenic trait that should respond well to natural selection, selective management, and breeding.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by the finding of 67 genes involved with relatively flat effect size distribution.

claim: The Central European droughts in the years 2018 and 2019 caused severe water stress in many forest tree species, leading to the die-off of many trees.
source: The Central European droughts in the years 2018 and 2019 caused severe water stress in many forest tree species, leading to the die-off of many trees (Schuldt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Schuldt et al., 2020.

claim: European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) is one of the most common deciduous tree species in Central Europe.
source: As one of the most common deciduous tree species in Central Europe, F. sylvatica is of great ecological importance
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Beech forests are a habitat for more than 6000 different animal and plant species.
source: beech forests are a habitat for more than 6000 different animal and plant species (Brunet et al., 2010; Dorow et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Brunet et al., 2010 and Dorow et al., 2010.

claim: The forestry use of beech in 2017 generated a turnover of more than €1 billion in Germany alone.
source: The forestry use of beech in 2017 generated a turnover of more than €1 billion in Germany alone (Thünen_Institute, 2020)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Thünen_Institute, 2020.

claim: Official reports on drought damage in beech recorded 62% of trees with rolled leaves and 20–30% of small leaves, mainly in the crown, resulting in 7% of badly damaged or dead trees.
source: Official reports on drought damage in beech recorded 62% of trees with rolled leaves and 20–30% of small leaves, mainly in the crown, resulting in 7% of badly damaged or dead trees.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction citing official reports.

claim: Mainly medium- to old-aged trees were affected by drought stress (>60 years).
source: As shown before (Bressem, 2008), mainly medium- to old-aged trees were affected by drought stress (>60 years).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Bressem, 2008.

claim: Under favourable conditions, beech is a competitive and shade-tolerant tree species, dominating mixed stands.
source: Under favourable conditions, beech is a competitive and shade-tolerant tree species, dominating mixed stands (Pretzsch et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Pretzsch et al., 2013.

claim: High genetic diversity within populations supports adaptation to local conditions in beech.
source: High genetic diversity within populations supports adaptation to local conditions (Kreyling et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Kreyling et al., 2012.

claim: Significant differences between local populations in tolerance to various stress factors such as early frost, drought, or air pollution are known in beech.
source: Significant differences between local populations in tolerance to various stress factors such as early frost (Czajkowski and Bolte, 2006), drought (Cocozza et al., 2016; Harter et al., 2015), or air pollution (Müller-Stark, 1985) are known.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: The distribution of F. sylvatica is mainly limited by water availability as the tree does not tolerate particularly wet or dry conditions.
source: The distribution of F. sylvatica is mainly limited by water availability as the tree does not tolerate particularly wet or dry conditions (Sutmöller et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Sutmöller et al., 2008.

claim: Crown deterioration is a significant indicator for drought damage in beech trees.
source: Using crown deterioration as a significant indicator for drought damage (Choat et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Choat et al., 2018.

claim: Not all trees in a beech stand were equally damaged or healthy, with damage occurring in a mosaic-like pattern.
source: not all trees in a beech stand were equally damaged or healthy. The damage occurred rather in a mosaic-like pattern instead.
evidence: This observation is described in the introduction based on field observations.

claim: Apparently completely healthy trees immediately neighboured severely damaged ones and vice versa.
source: apparently completely healthy trees immediately neighboured severely damaged ones and vice versa.
evidence: This observation is described in the introduction based on field observations.

claim: More than 200 neighbouring pairs of trees with extreme phenotypes were identified for the study.
source: We identified more than 200 neighbouring pairs of trees with extreme phenotypes
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the study design.

claim: The sampling sites were divided into two groups by a temperature gradient in principal component analysis.
source: When summarising the climatic conditions from 1950 to 2019 for the sampling sites in a principal component analysis (PCA), the sites were divided into two groups by axis 1, a temperature gradient.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Taunus mountain sites grouped with those from the northern part of Hessen, while the Rhein-Main plain clustered with the Odenwald sites.
source: The Taunus mountain sites grouped with those from the northern part of Hessen, while the Rhein-Main plain clustered with the Odenwald sites (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All local conditions changed substantially and similarly in the direction and extent of warmer and drier conditions when comparing the climate from the 1950s with the decade from 2010 to 2019.
source: Comparing the climate from the 1950s, when most of the trees sampled were already in place, with the decade from 2010 to 2019, showed that all local conditions changed substantially and similarly in the direction and extent of warmer and drier conditions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The steepest temperature increase occurred in the 1980s.
source: The steepest temperature increase occurred in the 1980s, while precipitation patterns mainly changed in the last decade (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Precipitation patterns mainly changed in the last decade.
source: The steepest temperature increase occurred in the 1980s, while precipitation patterns mainly changed in the last decade (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mean January daily minimum temperature at the sampling sites increased by 1.49°C from −2.64°C (s.d. 1.68°C) in the 1950s to −1.15°C (s.d. 2.50°C) during the last decade.
source: the mean January daily minimum temperature at the sampling sites increased by 1.49°C from −2.64°C (s.d. 1.68°C) in the 1950s to −1.15°C (s.d. 2.50°C) during the last decade.
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific temperature data.

claim: The mean August daily maximum temperatures increased by 2.37°C from 22.06°C (s.d. 1.95°C) to 24.43°C (s.d. 2.35°C).
source: The mean August daily maximum temperatures increased even more by 2.37°C from 22.06°C (s.d. 1.95°C) to 24.43°C (s.d. 2.35°C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific temperature data.

claim: Mean annual precipitation decreased by 40.5 mm or 5.5% from 741.2 mm (s.d. 85.8 mm) to 700.7 mm (s.d. 70.9 mm).
source: Simultaneously, mean annual precipitation decreased by 40.5 mm or 5.5% from 741.2 mm (s.d. 85.8 mm) to 700.7 mm (s.d. 70.9 mm).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific precipitation data.

claim: Most of the precipitation loss (84%) occurred during the main growth period between April and September, with a decrease of 33.9 mm from 410.4 mm (s.d. 36.1 mm) to 376.5 mm (s.d. 25.6 mm).
source: Most of the precipitation loss (84%) occurred during the main growth period between April and September, with a decrease of 33.9 mm from 410.4 mm (s.d. 36.1 mm) to 376.5 mm (s.d. 25.6 mm).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific precipitation data.

claim: The main growth period of beech from April to September became increasingly drier compared to the beginning of the 1990s, with up to 30 mm more evaporation per month.
source: Mean monthly evaporation potential, available from 1991 onwards, showed that, compared to the beginning of the 1990s, the main growth period of beech from April to September became increasingly drier, with up to 30 mm more evaporation per month.
evidence: This is stated in the results with evaporation data.

claim: The years 2018 and 2019 were not outliers, but rather part of a long-term, accelerating trend in drought dynamics.
source: The drought dynamics suggested that the years 2018 and 2019 were not outliers, but rather part of a long-term, accelerating trend (Figure 1C), following the overall global pattern (Büntgen et al., 2021; Trenberth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1C and citations.

claim: There was a strong negative correlation (r = 0.695) between the drought strength during the main growth period (Apr–Sept) and a proxy for (green) leaf cover (leaf area index [LAI]) for the sampled plots in the years 2015–2019.
source: There was a strong negative correlation (r = 0.695) between the drought strength during the main growth period (Apr– Sept) and a proxy for (green) leaf cover (leaf area index [LAI]) for the sampled plots in the years 2015–2019 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a correlation coefficient and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Leaf loss and dried leaves are good indicators for drought stress.
source: This observation suggested that leaf loss and dried leaves are good indicators for drought stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between drought and LAI.

claim: The mean distance between paired trees was 5.1 m (s.d. 3.4 m).
source: The mean distance between paired trees was 5.1 m (s.d. 3.4 m, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Healthy and damaged trees within each tree pair did not differ significantly in trunk circumference, tree height, canopy closure, and competition index.
source: Phenotypic measurements generally confirmed the study design and selection of trees: healthy and damaged trees within each tree pair did not differ significantly in trunk circumference, tree height, canopy closure, and competition index (Figure 2A–D, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A-D and Supplementary file 1B.

claim: The quantity of dried leaves and leaf loss differed substantially between damaged and healthy trees.
source: As expected, and confirming the assignment of damage status, the quantity of dried leaves and leaf loss differed substantially between damaged and healthy ones (Figure 2E, F, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2E, F and Supplementary file 1B.

claim: Four DNA pools were created for Pool-GWAS: damaged individuals from the Southern part (dSouth), healthy individuals from the South (hSouth), damaged North (dNorth), and healthy North (hNorth).
source: For a subsample of 300 out of the 402 sampled beech trees, we generated four DNA pools from two climatically distinct regions (North and South Hessen, Figure 1B), contrasting trees that were either healthy or highly drought damaged, respectively (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the pool construction.

claim: The 'South' pools consisted of 100 individuals each, whereas the 'North' pools contained 50 individuals each.
source: The 'South' pools consisted of 100 individuals each, whereas the 'North' pools contained 50 individuals each.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the pool composition.

claim: More than 96% of the reads mapped against the repeat-masked chromosome-level beech reference genome.
source: More than 96% of the reads mapped against the repeat-masked chromosome-level beech reference genome (accession no. PRJNA450822).
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the sequencing data.

claim: After filtering, allele frequencies for 9.6 million SNPs were scored.
source: After filtering the alignment for quality and a coverage between 15× and 70×, and removing indels, allele frequencies for 9.6 million SNPs were scored.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the SNP calling.

claim: All 100 individuals from the North population were additionally individually resequenced to ~20× coverage each.
source: All 100 individuals from the North population were additionally individually resequenced to ~20× coverage each
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the individual resequencing.

claim: Linkage disequilibrium fell to r² ~ 0.3 within <120 bp, which means that genome positions such a distance apart are on average effectively unlinked.
source: The plot of LD r² against the distance from the focal SNP showed that LD fell to r² ~ 0.3 within <120 bp, which means that genome positions such a distance apart are on average effectively unlinked (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The PCA on SNP variation of the individually resequenced trees from the North population explained 12.3% of accumulated variation on the first two axes.
source: The PCA on SNP variation of the individually resequenced trees from the North population explained 12.3% of accumulated variation on the first two axes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Trees from the same sampling site (within the North population) did not tend to cluster together.
source: Trees from the same sampling site (within the North population) did not tend to cluster together (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: FST estimates among pools for non-overlapping 1 kb windows were virtually identical among healthy/damaged pools within region as compared to between regions.
source: FST estimates among pools for non-overlapping 1 kb windows were virtually identical among healthy/damaged pools within region as compared to between regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Trees within a phenotypic class were genomically not more similar than between classes.
source: Trees within a phenotypic class were genomically not more similar than between classes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3, ANOSIM R = −0.008, p=0.76, 9999 permutations).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and ANOSIM statistics.

claim: Some of the 106 SNPs were in close physical proximity (<120 bp) and thus probably linked.
source: Some of the 106 SNPs were in close physical proximity (<120 bp) and thus probably linked.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on the LD analysis.

claim: Taking linkage into account, 80 independent genomic regions were associated with the drought damage status.
source: Taking this into account, 80 independent genomic regions were associated with the drought damage status.
evidence: This is stated in the results after accounting for linkage.

claim: None of the significantly differentiated SNP loci was mutually fixed.
source: None of the significantly differentiated SNP loci was mutually fixed
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the nature of the associated SNPs.

claim: The observed allele frequency differences between healthy and damaged trees at associated loci ranged between 0.12 and 0.51.
source: the observed allele frequency differences between healthy and damaged trees at associated loci ranged between 0.12 and 0.51 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Of the 106 significant SNPs, 24 were found in 20 protein coding genes.
source: Of the 106 significant SNPs, 24 were found in 20 protein coding genes (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Table 1.

claim: Forty-nine genes were the closest genes to the remaining 82 SNPs.
source: Forty-nine genes were the closest genes to the remaining 82 SNPs.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the gene annotation.

claim: For 61 of these genes, the best BLAST hit was with a tree, mainly from the Fagales genera Quercus and Castanea.
source: For 61 of these genes, the best BLAST hit was with a tree, mainly from the Fagales genera Quercus and Castanea (Table 1, Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Table 1 and Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Among the 24 SNPs in genes, 13 non-synonymous changes were observed.
source: Among the 24 SNPs in genes, we observed 13 non-synonymous changes.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the SNP effects.

claim: In 11 of the non-synonymous changes, the alternate allele was associated with the damaged phenotype and only in two cases with the healthy phenotype.
source: In 11 of these changes, the alternate allele was associated with the damaged phenotype and only in two cases with the healthy phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the phenotype associations.

claim: Three of the non-synonymous substitutions resulted in a stop codon.
source: Three of the non-synonymous substitutions resulted in a stop codon.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1.

claim: Of the remaining 10 non-synonymous substitutions, 8 exchanges caused a major change in amino acid characteristics and thus probably in protein folding or function.
source: Of the remaining 10, 8 exchanges caused a major change in amino acid characteristics and thus probably in protein folding or function (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Table 1.

claim: One gene, a PB1 domain-containing protein tyrosine kinase, contained four non-synonymous changes, suggesting that the allele version associated with the damaged phenotype lost its function.
source: One gene, a PB1 domain-containing protein tyrosine kinase, contained four non-synonymous changes, suggesting that the allele version associated with the damaged phenotype lost its function (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Table 1.

claim: From the 20 genes with significant SNPs, functional information could be obtained from the UniProt database for 14.
source: From the 20 genes with significant SNPs, functional information could be obtained from the UniProt database for 14 (Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Of the 14 genes with functional information, 10 genes were associated in previous studies with either environmental stress response (two) or specifically with drought stress response (eight).
source: Of these, 10 genes were associated in previous studies with either environmental stress response (two) or specifically with drought stress response (eight; Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Supplementary file 1C.

claim: Of the 49 predicted genes closest to the remaining significant SNPs, 16 could be reliably annotated.
source: Of the 49 predicted genes closest to the remaining significant SNPs (Table 1), 16 could be reliably annotated (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Supplementary file 1B.

claim: Of the 16 reliably annotated genes closest to significant SNPs, 12 had been directly related to drought in previous studies, while three were previously associated with other environmental stress responses.
source: Twelve had been directly related to drought in previous studies, while three were previously associated with other environmental stress responses (Supplementary file 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Supplementary file 1C.

claim: 70 loci proved to be suitable for reliable genotyping with an SNP assay after excluding loci due to technical reasons and filtering for genotyping success.
source: After excluding loci due to technical reasons and filtering for genotyping success, 70 loci proved to be suitable for reliable genotyping with an SNP assay.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the SNP assay development.

claim: On average, each of the 95 individuals was successfully genotyped at 67.7 loci (96.7%).
source: On average, each of the 95 individuals was successfully genotyped at 67.7 loci (96.7%).
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the genotyping success.

claim: By selecting the 20 most informative SNPs, the machine learning method identified four different clusters.
source: By selecting the 20 most informative SNPs, the method identified four different clusters.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the machine learning analysis.

claim: Forty-seven resistant trees were correctly assigned to cluster 1 and 2, while nine susceptible trees were falsely allocated there.
source: Forty-seven resistant trees were correctly assigned to cluster 1 and 2, while nine susceptible trees were falsely allocated there.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the clustering results.

claim: Thirty-nine susceptible trees were correctly assigned in clusters 3 and 4, while three resistant trees also fell in these categories.
source: Thirty-nine susceptible trees were correctly assigned in clusters 3 and 4, while three resistant trees also fell in these categories.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the clustering results.

claim: 88% of the 98 trees could be correctly classified according to their observed phenotype using the machine learning approach.
source: In this way, 88% of the 98 trees could be correctly classified according to their observed phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the prediction accuracy.

claim: Over the last two decades, increasing drought periods caused severe damage to European forests.
source: Over the last two decades, increasing drought periods caused severe damage to European forests (Schuldt et al., 2020; Etzold et al., 2019; Pretzsch et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with multiple citations.

claim: Conifers seem to suffer the most from drought, but deciduous trees were also strongly affected.
source: Conifers seem to suffer the most, but deciduous trees were also strongly affected (Schuldt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Schuldt et al., 2020.

claim: More than a third of the trees were already in place at the beginning of the 1950-2019 period based on trunk circumference age estimates.
source: Roughly estimating the tree age from their trunk circumference (Bošeľa et al., 2014), more than a third of the trees were already in place at the beginning of this period.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Bošeľa et al., 2014.

claim: About 60% of the trees were recruited prior to the acceleration of temperature change from the 1980s onwards.
source: About 60% were recruited prior to the acceleration of temperature change from the 1980s onwards.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on age estimates.

claim: Trees in the mountainous regions of the study area today experience climatic conditions comparable to those experienced by lowland trees in the 1950s.
source: As a result, trees in the mountainous regions of the study area today experience climatic conditions comparable to those experienced by lowland trees in the 1950s
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on climate data analysis.

claim: Lowland trees now experience a climate that used to be typical for regions much further South.
source: which in turn now experience a climate that used to be typical for regions much further South.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on climate data analysis.

claim: Current conditions exceed the reaction norm of some previously locally well-adapted genotypes with detrimental consequences for their fitness.
source: Given the documented propensity of beech for local adaptation (Gárate‐Escamilla et al., 2019; Pluess et al., 2016; Aranda et al., 2015), including drought (Bolte et al., 2016), it is therefore conceivable that current conditions exceed the reaction norm of some previously locally well-adapted genotypes with detrimental consequences for their fitness.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations supporting local adaptation.

claim: If the trend of an increasingly drier vegetation period persists, this will likely affect an even larger proportion of the currently growing beeches.
source: If the trend of an increasingly drier vegetation period persists, this will likely affect an even larger proportion of the currently growing beeches.
evidence: This is a prediction stated in the discussion based on the observed trends.

claim: Evolutionary genomics will be indispensable to predict and manage the impact of global change on biodiversity.
source: Evolutionary genomics will be indispensable to predict and manage the impact of global change on biodiversity (Waldvogel et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Waldvogel et al., 2020.

claim: Pool-GWAS approaches have proven to be useful in guiding conservation management for partially managed (tree) species.
source: As already shown for other partially managed (tree) species (Stocks et al., 2019), in particular pool-GWAS approaches (Endler et al., 2016) have proven to be useful in guiding conservation management.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to Stocks et al., 2019 and Endler et al., 2016.

claim: The strictly pairwise sampling design avoided many pitfalls of GWAS studies, arising from cryptic population structure and shared ancestry.
source: Our strictly pairwise sampling design avoided many pitfalls of GWAS studies, arising, for example, from cryptic population structure and shared ancestry (Hoban et al., 2016; Wellenreuther and Hansson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to Hoban et al., 2016 and Wellenreuther and Hansson, 2016.

claim: The mean distance between sampled paired trees of about 5 m assured that their roots systems largely overlapped.
source: In the present study, however, the mean distance between sampled paired trees of about 5 m assured that their roots systems largely overlapped.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the distance measurements.

claim: Any phenotypical misclassification due to microspatial differences would have rather dissimulated the genotypic differences found in GWAS than enhanced them artificially.
source: Please note that any phenotypical misclassification due to such microspatial differences would have rather dissimulated the genotypic differences found in GWAS than enhanced them artificially.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a logical inference about potential biases.

claim: No population structure was found among the sampling sites, as expected from previous studies.
source: As expected from previous studies (Rajendra et al., 2014), we found no population structure among the sampling sites.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Rajendra et al., 2014.

claim: The observed very short average LD in F. sylvatica indicates that polymorphisms associated with the two phenotypes were likely old-standing genetic variation.
source: These findings were in line with the observed very short average LD in F. sylvatica, indicating that polymorphisms associated with the two phenotypes were likely old-standing genetic variation (Harris and Nielsen, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Harris and Nielsen, 2013.

claim: SNPs with short LD are mostly detached from the background in which they arose and are therefore often the actual causal variants or at least in very close proximity.
source: Moreover, such SNPs are mostly detached from the background in which they arose and they are therefore often the actual causal variants or at least in very close proximity (Schaid et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Schaid et al., 2018.

claim: The high proportion of non-synonymous significant SNPs within genes underlines that the associated SNPs are likely causal variants or in very close proximity.
source: This observation is underlined by the high proportion of non-synonymous significant SNPs within genes, which in most cases caused substitution to an amino acid with different properties or even premature termination.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the SNP annotation results.

claim: Deviant variants with likely substantial functional or conformational changes in the resulting proteins may be selectively neutral or nearly neutral under ancestral benign conditions, but may become selectively relevant under changing conditions.
source: Such deviant variants with likely substantial functional or conformational changes in the resulting proteins may be selectively neutral or nearly neutral under ancestral benign conditions, but may become selectively relevant under changing conditions (Paaby and Rockman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Paaby and Rockman, 2014.

claim: Most of the allelic variants associated with a healthy phenotype were also the variants in the reference genome.
source: Interestingly, most of the allelic variants associated with a healthy phenotype were also the variants in the reference genome.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with the reference genome.

claim: The reference genome individual is a more than 300-year-old tree standing at a particularly dry site on a rocky outcrop where precipitation swiftly runs off.
source: This might be due to the choice of the F. sylvatica individual from which the reference genome was gained (Mishra et al., 2018). This more than 300-year-old individual is standing at a particularly dry site on a rocky outcrop on the rim of a scarp where precipitation swiftly runs off.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Mishra et al., 2018.

claim: Trees at dry sites were likely selected for drought tolerance.
source: Trees at such sites were likely selected for drought tolerance.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference about selection.

claim: The climatic variation covered by the sampling sites for this study is representative for large parts of the species range.
source: In addition, the climatic variation covered by the sampling sites for this study is representative for large parts of the species range (Baumbach et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Baumbach et al., 2019.

claim: The relatively limited population structure over large parts of the species range, together with the propensity for long-range gene flow, suggests that the genomic variation responsible for drought tolerance identified here is widely distributed.
source: The relatively limited population structure over large parts of the species range (Magri et al., 2006), together with the propensity for long-range gene flow (Belmonte et al., 2008), suggested that the genomic variation responsible for drought tolerance identified here is widely distributed (Lander et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to Magri et al., 2006, Belmonte et al., 2008, and Lander et al., 2021.

claim: None of the genes found in this study was involved in a transcriptomic study on drought response in beech saplings.
source: None of the genes found here was involved in a transcriptomic study on drought response in beech saplings (Müller et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Müller et al., 2017.

claim: Most of the reliably annotated genes with or close to SNP loci significantly associated with drought phenotypes had putative homologs in other plant species previously shown to be involved in drought or different environmental stress response.
source: However, most of the reliably annotated genes with or close to SNP loci significantly associated with drought phenotypes had putative homologs in other plant species previously shown to be involved in drought or different environmental stress response (for citations, see Supplementary file 1C, D).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to Supplementary file 1C, D.

claim: The involvement of in total 67 genes, together with the relatively flat effect size distribution, suggests that drought resistance in F. sylvatica is a moderately polygenic trait.
source: The involvement of in total 67 genes, together with the relatively flat effect size distribution, suggested that drought resistance in F. sylvatica is a moderately polygenic trait, which should respond well to artificial breeding attempts and natural selection.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the number of genes and effect sizes.

claim: A moderately polygenic trait should respond well to artificial breeding attempts and natural selection.
source: The involvement of in total 67 genes, together with the relatively flat effect size distribution, suggested that drought resistance in F. sylvatica is a moderately polygenic trait, which should respond well to artificial breeding attempts and natural selection.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference about breeding potential.

claim: It is likely that more yet undetected loci contribute to the respective phenotypes given the relatively strict threshold criteria.
source: However, given the relatively strict threshold criteria, it is likely that more yet undetected loci contribute to the respective phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference about undetected loci.

claim: The low LD in beech predicts that an adaptation to drought will not compromise genome-wide genetic diversity and thus adaptation potential to other stressors.
source: The low LD in beech predicts that an adaptation to drought will not compromise genome-wide genetic diversity and thus adaptation potential to other stressors.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a prediction based on the LD findings.

claim: The analysis confirmed that the identified alleles are widespread throughout the sampled range and not locally specific.
source: The analysis confirmed that we mainly identified alleles widespread throughout the sampled range and not locally specific.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the validation analysis.

claim: There is still adaptive potential for drought adaptation in the species, as indicated by the observation that trees with the highest predictive values showed no loss of heterozygosity.
source: Besides, we confirmed a considerable level of genetic variation in the sampled regions. The observation that trees with the highest predictive values showed no loss of heterozygosity indicated that there is still adaptive potential for drought adaptation in the species (Gienapp et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to Gienapp et al., 2017.

claim: The SNP assay can support the choice of seed trees for reforestations.
source: With the SNP assay, we therefore created a tool that can (i) support the choice of seed trees for reforestations
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential application.

claim: The SNP assay can provide decision guidance for selective logging.
source: (ii) provide decision guidance for selective logging
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential application.

claim: The SNP assay can monitor whether natural selection on this quantitative trait is already acting in the species.
source: (iii) monitor whether natural selection on this quantitative trait is already acting in the species.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential application.

claim: The current study can serve as a starting point for molecular and physiological research on how the identified loci or variants may, alone or in concert, confer resilience or tolerance to a range of drought stress symptoms.
source: The current study can also serve as a starting point for molecular and physiological research on how the identified loci or variants may, alone or in concert, confer resilience or tolerance to a range of drought stress symptoms.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a potential future direction.

claim: In August/early September 2019, leaf tissue of 402 F. sylvatica trees from 32 locations in Hessen/Germany was sampled.
source: In August/early September 2019, we sampled leaf tissue of 402 F. sylvatica trees from 32 locations in Hessen/Germany (set 1, Figure 1)
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: 300 of the 402 sampled trees were used for the (pool)GWAS analysis.
source: of which 300 were used for the (pool)GWAS analysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: An additional 53 trees were sampled in August 2020, plus 52 trees from four sites, which made up the confirmation set.
source: 43, plus additional 53 trees which were sampled in August 2020, additional 52 trees from four sites were sampled (set 2, Figure 1) which made up the confirmation set.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The pairs consisted of one tree with heavy damage of the crown (lost or rolled up, dried leaves) and one with an unaffected crown.
source: The pairs consisted of one tree with heavy damage of the crown (lost or rolled up, dried leaves) and one with an unaffected crown, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the sampling design.

claim: The pairs were chosen such that the two trees were mutually the closest neighbours with contrasting damage status, free from apparent mechanical damage, fungal infestations, or other signs of illness, and similar in tree height, trunk circumference, light availability, and canopy closure.
source: The pairs were a priori chosen such that the two trees were (i) mutually the closest neighbours with contrasting damage status (i.e. no other tree in the direct sight line), (ii) free from apparent mechanical damage, fungal infestations, or other signs of illness, similar (iii) in tree height, (iv) trunk circumference, (v) light availability, and (vi) canopy closure.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the sampling criteria.

claim: Each pair was situated at least 30 m from the closest forest edge.
source: In addition, each pair was situated at least 30 m from the closest forest edge.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the sampling criteria.

claim: Monthly daily mean minimum and maximum temperature values and precipitation data were obtained for the 1 × 1 km grid cells harbouring the sampling sites for the period between 1950 and 2019.
source: Monthly daily mean minimum and maximum temperature values and precipitation data were obtained for the 1 × 1 km grid cells harbouring the sampling sites for the period between 1950 and 2019.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing climate data collection.

claim: Climate and remote sensing data is publicly available from https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/grids_germany/monthly/.
source: The data is publicly available from https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/grids_germany/monthly/.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: LAI data for the grid cells was obtained from Copernicus for the period 2014–2019, considering only the month of August.
source: LAI data for the above grid cells was obtained from Copernicus (http://www.copernicus.eu) for the period 2014–2019, considering only the month of August.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: DNA was extracted from 12.5 mm² of a single leaf from each tree following the NucleoMag Plant Kit protocol.
source: DNA was extracted from 12.5 mm² of a single leaf from each tree following the NucleoMag Plant Kit (Macherey Nagel, Düren, Germany) protocol.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: An improved version of the recently published reference genome for the European beech was used.
source: We used an improved version of the recently published reference genome for the European beech (Mishra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation to Mishra et al., 2018.

claim: Contiguity was improved to chromosome level using Hi-C reads with the help of the allhic software.
source: Contiguity was improved to chromosome level using Hi-C reads with the help of the allhic software after excluding the probable organelle backbones from the earlier assembly that was generated from the Illumina-corrected PacBio reads using Canu assembler (Mishra et al., 2021) accession no. PRJNA450822.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation to Mishra et al., 2021.
